We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4{x}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{2x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+1)(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2})(8x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}}{2}-4\int x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{2x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{2x}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{2x}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2x}}{4}+D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}}{4}(2x-1)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}}{2}-4(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{4}(2x-1)+D) \\  & =\frac{(4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}}{2}-{e}^{2x}(2x-1)-4D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}(4{x}^{2}-4x+3)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-4D.$
